# Aidecis

> Aidecis is the decision intelligence and control layer for consequential procurement and supply-chain decisions. It gives one authority model and one decision record to every consequential procurement and supply-chain decision, whoever or whatever takes it: a company's people, its own algorithms, its vendors' agents and Aidecis's own agents. The record runs from the first signal through execution and is linked to the outcome.

Aidecis does not replace ERP systems such as SAP, access control or AI model governance tools. It sets who and what may decide each consequential decision, before it runs, and keeps one record of it across every system and vendor.

Key facts:

- Category: the decision intelligence and control layer for consequential procurement and supply-chain decisions; one authority model and one decision record across people, client algorithms and vendors' agents.
- Demo: the public demo runs on fictional data (De Boer BV). Capabilities and live connections are agreed for each project.
- Coverage: enforced before execution through the Aidecis gateway; observed and reconciled after execution for registered actors outside it.
- Two levels of control. Enforced: the action runs only through the Aidecis gateway with a single-use grant, so Aidecis can prove it was authorised before it ran. Observed: an agent or algorithm that writes in its own system with its own credentials is detected afterwards from the systems' change records, matched against its registered role, limits and mode, recorded, and flagged within minutes if it went outside them. Observed control does not prevent an action; it shows it.
- Market vocabulary: operating models human-to-agent, agent-to-human and agent-to-agent (agent-to-agent chains are not offered at launch); autonomy scale 1 assisted, 2 co-adaptive, 3 self-directing, 4 self-managing. The client's maturity in each decision family caps how far automation may go. A decision moves up the scale only when its performance is stable, it has a named owner, its exception rate is accepted, its actions are reversible, and monitoring and rollback are in place; otherwise it moves back down. Market scenario (WEF and Accenture, 2026), not an Aidecis result: most supply-chain domains are at autonomy level 1 to 2 now and are expected to reach 3.5 or more over the next five years and beyond.
- Decision modes: people decide (agents prepare evidence and options); hybrid (a bot proposes and a person approves, or the bot decides within a set limit); bot (only reversible actions within approved limits, with monitoring and a way to stop).
- Lifecycle: propose, evaluate (authority, constraints and policy), approve or escalate to the accountable owner, execute through a customer-side gateway, learn from the recorded outcome.
- Architecture: policies and decision logic are managed in the Aidecis European cloud. A gateway runs inside the customer's IT environment and carries out only actions permitted by policy and within the proposer's authority, in systems such as ERP, WMS, TMS, MES and quality systems. In the demo, the gateway runs against simulated systems.
- Continuity package with every subscription: export in open formats, an open-source ledger verifier (https://github.com/aidecistech/aidecis-ledger-verifier), escrow of the control kernel and gateway, and exit assistance; a dedicated control plane is an option.
- Vendor-trust pack, available on request: security, privacy and AI-governance documentation mapped to ISO/IEC 42001 and to the client's EU AI Act deployer duties.
- European application with European data residency.
- Getting started: a paid pilot or evidence sprint on one decision type, EUR 16,000 to 24,000 (10 to 15 engineer days at EUR 1,600). Fixed deliverables at weeks 0, 2 and 4, a shadow report at week 8 and an assist report at week 12. The first slice is read-only. Each pilot has one hard measure in the buyer's own terms, such as response time to a disruption, premium freight spend, stockout hours or price variance.
- Published prices, indicative and excluding taxes: subscription EUR 45,000 per year, including the first site and two regions; extra sites EUR 4,750 per site per year for sites 2 to 50 and EUR 1,850 per site from site 51; warehouses EUR 600 each per year; implementation EUR 1,600 per day, 50 days base plus 0.25 day per extra site; no per-user fee. Example: 10 sites cost EUR 87,750 per year with implementation of about EUR 83,600; 50 sites cost EUR 277,750 per year with implementation of about EUR 99,600.
- Company: Aidecis is an Angeleus SLU company, based in Escaldes-Engordany, Andorra.
- Languages on the website: English, Spanish and Dutch.

## Main pages

- [Home](https://www.aidecis.com/): what Aidecis is, people/bots/hybrid decisions, the decision lifecycle, architecture and how to start.
- [Use cases and decision library](https://www.aidecis.com/use-cases.html): the twelve families of consequential decisions Aidecis governs, starting with procurement and supply chain (procurement, logistics, planning, demand, production, quality, maintenance, trading, warehousing, energy, HSE); finance and close-out follows in a later phase. Twelve worked use cases.
- [Decision accountability](https://www.aidecis.com/accountability.html): ten common supply-chain decision scenarios and how authority, policy, approval, execution and outcome are kept in one chain.
- [Benefits and business case](https://www.aidecis.com/benefits.html): a calculator for the pilot, subscription and implementation at the published prices, and a business case with your own assumptions, net of review effort and compute, with today's response time to a disruption as the resilience baseline.
- [Industries](https://www.aidecis.com/industries.html): how the same decision accountability applies across eleven industries.
- [Security and data](https://www.aidecis.com/security.html): architecture, data flows, deployment options, EU hosting and subprocessors, control coverage, continuity and exit, and certification status (no certification claimed; penetration test scheduled for December 2026).
- [Company](https://www.aidecis.com/company.html): the company (an Angeleus SLU company in Andorra), how Aidecis works with clients, and how case studies are published.
- [Team](https://www.aidecis.com/team.html): the founding team and the advisory board.
- [Contact](https://www.aidecis.com/contact.html): ask a question, request a demo, or ask about a pilot or evidence sprint.

## Twelve decision families and their flagship decisions

1. Logistics and transport: expedite freight after disruption
2. Planning and inventory: inventory reallocation between sites
3. Demand and customer commitments: customer promise and backorder priority
4. Procurement and supply: ingredient or material price beyond envelope
5. Quality and product compliance: quality hold, release or substitute
6. Production and operations: production rescheduling
7. Maintenance and assets: unplanned failure, run reduced or stop to repair
8. Trading and commodity positions: buy or sell a cargo, with its downstream chain
9. Warehousing and terminals: tank or storage allocation
10. Energy and utilities: curtail or shift production on an energy price spike
11. Health, safety and environment: permit or emission limit exceedance
12. Finance and close-out (later phase): invoice variance, claim and close-out

The full decision library (71 decision types) is used with clients in a guided decision assessment inside the Aidecis platform; contact Aidecis to book one.
